look_here_first: FIRST photograph a MATURE UPPER-STEM NODE: the sessile leaf has two rounded, conspicuously HEART-SHAPED CLASPING auricles which wrap the stem. Check stiff, relatively broad upper leaves and spreading branch angles. Unlike S. oblongifolium, the leaf base is deeply cordate, not merely rounded or slightly clasping. IMPORTANT: S. patens var. patens ALSO has stalked glands, so gland presence cannot independently separate it from aromatic aster.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Against S. oblongifolium: look at how strongly upper leaves clasp the stem—S. patens upper leaves are truly cordate-amplexicaul/auriculate, whereas S. oblongifolium has relatively short oblong leaves that are often only rounded or mildly clasping. Glandular phyllaries occur in S. patens too, with substantial varietal variation; gland presence is NOT an exclusive oblongifolium character.
